statements: The Panel described Ri Yong Min as managing an approximately 15-person IT-worker group.

The Russian Federation replied that most relevant DPRK migrant workers—including Pak Kwang Hyok and Ri Yong Min—had left by the end of 2019; it attributed delayed remaining departures after employment termination to pandemic transport suspension.

sources.support: Evidence class: official UN Panel report relaying Member State information with host-state response. Source-qualified support: The Panel described an approximately 50-person Vladivostok IT-worker group managed by Ri Kyong Sik and Pak Kwang Hyok, with Ri in charge of six software-development teams. It described a separate Munitions Industry Department-subordinate group led by Jang Ho Yong and a third approximately 15-person group managed by Ri Yong Min. The Russian Federation replied that the majority of the relevant DPRK migrant workers, including Ri Kyong Sik, Pak Kwang Hyok, and Ri Yong Min, had left by the end of 2019; remaining departures were reportedly delayed after employment termination because transport was suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic
